hypothesis: Lowering the InfoNCE temperature hyperparameter from 0.2 to 0.1 will increase contrastive penalty on hard negatives, resulting in better feature discriminability within the short 50-epoch pretraining budget.
rationale: In iter 5, switching to InfoNCE with temperature 0.2 yielded a massive jump to 0.5141 val acc. However, SimCLR literature demonstrates that lower temperature values (around 0.07 to 0.1) are critical for hardness-aware loss scaling, preventing easy negatives from dominating the gradients and accelerating representations learning for complex 100-class datasets like CIFAR-100.
expected_effect: Stronger gradient signal from hard negative pairs, leading to higher linear evaluation accuracy (> 0.5141).
change_summary: Decreased temperature default parameter from 0.2 to 0.1 in BarlowTwinsLoss (InfoNCE).
